title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults, quant profiles, unit-econ tooling
author: Marcus Lee
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token serving cost by automating sensible defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, introduce model-specific quantization profiles, and surface unit-economics in the Console so teams can safely tune for cost without regressions.

What this PR does: Adds an autotune service that computes recommended batching and caching defaults per route based on recent traffic histograms; introduces model-aware quantization profiles and a mapping layer so we can roll different quantization configs safely; and adds a Unit Economics dashboard and CLI tooling to estimate cost/latency trade-offs for candidate configs.

High level changes (single-pass summary):
- services/autotune: new service that reads recent route metrics, runs a fast heuristic optimizer and outputs policy suggestions to config-store. (Includes background worker, protobufs, and feature flag gating.)
- runtime: small runtime hooks to accept per-route default batch/caching hints and to annotate requests with applied policy for observability.
- model-profiles: quantization profile registry, onboarding scripts, and compatibility matrix for int8/4-bit candidates by architecture.
- console: Unit Economics dashboard (per-route view), config preview modal, and rollout assistant UI to apply suggestions as canary/beta.
- cli: new `redwood uecon estimate` command to compute expected unit-cost given traffic distribution and quant profile.
- tests/docs: integration tests for autotune worker, unit tests for registry, and docs + playbook for safe rollout.

Checklist: 
- [x] Autotune heuristic implementation and worker
- [x] Config-store write with audit log entries
- [x] Model quant profiles registry and validation tests
- [x] Console UI + permission gating
- [x] CLI estimate tool and docs
- [x] E2E tests for canary rollout path

Migration/Gating: The autotune service is behind a feature flag (autotune:uecon) and suggestions are non-destructive by default (they appear as suggestions in Console; operators must opt-in to apply). Quant profiles are additive and require explicit model pinning. The rollout assistant supports canary + automatic rollback on quality regressions.

Testing notes: CI runs unit, integration, and UI tests. A flaky integration test (runtime/kvcache-integration) failed on the first CI run due to a timing issue; I added a retry/backoff fixture and re-ran — CI passed on rerun. Load tests (internal perf-canary) show ~12-18% cost savings on sampled routes when autosuggests are applied conservatively (small batch increase + prefix caching).

Related: Linear ENG-9082 (autotune worker), ENG-9124 (unit-econ dashboard), Support ticket SUP-3321 for a customer request to estimate dedicated capacity savings.

Release notes:
- Added autotune service for batching/caching default suggestions
- Added model quantization profiles and compatibility registry
- Added Unit Economics dashboard and CLI estimate tool

Security: No new privileged data flows. Config writes are audited and require role-based permission.

Rollback plan: Disable feature flag and revert applied suggestions via the Console or stop the autotune worker.

review_comments: Sofia Hernandez: Nice work. Two questions: (1) How do we ensure suggestions don't increase 95th p99 latency for latency-sensitive routes? (2) Can we add a safety check to prevent applying aggressive batching on low-concurrency routes?

Marcus Lee: Answered — autotune computes cost/latency impact estimate and marks any suggestion that increases p99 latency by >5% as 'requires manual review'. Added low-concurrency guard to heuristics (min concurrent requests threshold).
Amit Patel: Please add an integration test that simulates prefix caching TTL churn. Also add an audit entry that includes previous policy snapshot.

Marcus Lee: Added test (tests/e2e/uecon_canary.test.ts) and config-store snapshot write. CI initially failed on runtime/kvcache-integration — added retry/backoff and increased timeout; re-ran CI and green.
Lena Zhou: Approving pending small nits in console copy and a11y labels. Marcus: addressed and pushed fixes.

notes_on_impact: Internal perf-canary tests show mean token-cost reduction 12-18% on sampled routes when suggestions applied conservatively; expected to be larger for routes with redundant prefix work. No observed regression in output quality during canary.
